name: Xuanzang's pilgrimage to India
summary: A young monk slips out of Tang China without permission to find better Buddhist texts. Sixteen years later he returns with 657 of them and dictates a record of 138 countries that maps India for China in detail.

stops.note: Leaves secretly; travel abroad has been forbidden.
Slips past the frontier guards at night.
Crosses the Gobi alone on an old red horse and nearly dies of thirst.
The first oasis beyond the desert.
The king of Gaochang begs him to stay and teach; he goes on hunger strike to be let go.
A Buddhist kingdom famous for its musicians.
Crosses the Tian Shan; many of his party die in the snow.
Received by the khagan of the Western Turks in his felt tent.
An oasis city on the road west.
A great trading city, not yet Buddhist.
The Nava Vihara monastery.
Sees the great standing Buddhas, then gilded.
Once a Buddhist heartland, now with many ruined monasteries.
Two years of study.
A centre of Buddhist sculpture.
Capital of King Harsha.
Birthplace of the Buddha, already in ruins.
The deer park at Sarnath where the Buddha first taught.
The tree of the enlightenment.
Studies under the abbot Silabhadra for five years.
A port where he hears of Sri Lanka but does not go.
The far south of his travels.
Harsha holds a great assembly in his honour.
Crosses the Pamirs; loses his elephant and many texts at a river crossing.
The western gate of the Tarim basin.
Writes to the emperor to ask pardon for having left.
Waits here for the emperor's reply.
Returns with 657 texts. Emperor Taizong asks him to write down everything he saw.
